unresolved.reason: Identifier mismatch: no unique Bao 2024 cadmium-nanoparticle mussel study was identified. The explicitly linked HMI anchor gives DOI 10.1093/jaoacint/qsae024, whose primary full text is a different article by Bruvold, Valdersnes, Loeschner and Bienfait on gold nanoparticle method validation. Do not publish that unrelated paper under the claimed Bao/cadmium title.

The bibliography supplies a generic description, without a jurisdiction, issuing body, instrument number, date or link. No uniquely identifiable original source was recovered. EU 2023/915 contains relevant tissue-specific limits, but it cannot silently stand in for the unidentified citation.

Official status and enacted Act 110 identified, but readable official enactment and effective-date text could not be retrieved after repeated timeouts/502 responses. Search excerpts were not accepted as a substitute for reading the law. Preserve pending until actual final text is read.
Exact cited Heavy Metal Index page returns HTTP 404 via direct retrieval; web access and exact-site search did not recover this resource. Do not silently substitute FDA sources or another HMI page.

Grouped WHO/FAO citation has no document title, URL or edition identifying food and irrigation benchmarks. Secondary papers repeat inconsistent units/bases. The primary FAO irrigation table reviewed lists lead 5.0 mg/L, not the claimed 0.5 mg/L, and cannot identify or verify this entire grouped reference.

Grouped reference includes a 2025 Scheduling Order without a date or docket number. The underlying exposé preprint reference 23 says December 2025, still without a docket number. The intended scheduling document was not identified; do not substitute a different pretrial order or a docket-count report. The 2024 transfer order and dated counts are verified but do not complete this grouped source review.

USDA’s official December 10 and 12, 2025 bulletins identify Directive 7221.1 Revision 4, Prior Labeling Approval. The current directive page and candidate official PDF returned 403 after repeated direct and web attempts. An exact Revision 3 (January 18, 2023) PDF is accessible on Spain’s agriculture ministry site, but it is superseded and was not silently substituted. Preserve pending for a readable Revision 4 text, especially current submission and inspection procedures.

The exact October 31, 2017 FDA In Brief announcement is identified by FDA’s current index and current SARMs page, but the original current slug returned 404 and the old FDA URL did not expose readable content. Preserve this numbered source as pending rather than replace it silently with a later warning. Current primary FDA overview supports a limited description of SARMs as illegally marketed unapproved drugs, not dietary supplements, but does not verify the complete original announcement.

Grouped citation only partly resolved: EU 2023/915 is identified and reviewed, but “national human-food maximum levels compiled in the HMTc regulatory register” does not identify jurisdictions, instruments, version or frozen register. Do not replace the entire group with the EU component. Israel values cannot be marked verified from the available local register alone.

No edition or complete identifiable OP chapter is supplied. The 2026 Official Publication requires access not available here; the freely accessible model PDF contains omissions and labeling excerpts, insufficient to certify the asserted absence of limits throughout AAFCO/NRC materials.

Homepage identifies a changing reference library, not a unique pet-food/per-analyte baseline with defined included documents, methods or version. No specific source can be matched to the bibliography without substituting an invented collection.

Exact-source access limitation reused from batch6-peptides-unresolved.json: the October 31, 2017 FDA In Brief announcement remains unavailable at its current 404 slug and old URL. FDA’s current primary overview was read and confirms the historical title and date, but is not substituted for the original. The page’s assertion that unapproved status places products beyond regulation is not supported by the current FDA overview.

Grouped reference remains unresolved: Thailand Notification 414 is identifiable and its FAO-hosted unofficial English translation gives supplement lead 1 mg/kg as prepared for consumption; GSO 193:2021 catalog identity was found but its paid numerical table was not read; Israel “FCS-2016” could not be tied to an exact primary instrument; the official Vietnamese QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT PDF could not be consistently retrieved for a verified numerical read. Do not silently replace the Israeli instrument or publish this four-country grouping as fully reviewed. None of the partial reads establishes a universal adult-body-weight premise.
